overall: The AG found the Somerville School Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely approve minutes and by missing the 10-day minutes-request deadline, ordered future compliance, declined the materials and extra-allegation claims, and ordered no further relief.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee stopped approving meeting minutes after July 27, 2020, until his February 2021 complaint, including minutes from August and September 2020 meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely approve numerous sets of meeting minutes in a timely manner.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee failed to respond to his February 9, 2021 request for meeting minutes within 10 calendar days.
allegations.key_passage: As the Committee did not send a response to Mr. Brown until 13 calendar days after he sent his initial request, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee failed to provide all handouts, slides and other meeting materials used at the same meetings; the AG declined, as this is a Public Records Law matter.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, failure to comply with that timeframe implicates the Public Records Law, which is outside the jurisdiction of the Division of Open Government.

allegations.summary: The request for further review raised allegations not included in the original complaint; the AG declined to review those additional allegations.
allegations.key_passage: Our office does not conduct broad audits of public bodies and will address only specific allegations made in an Open Meeting Law complaint.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law (no further relief ordered, since the Committee had by August 18 created, approved and sent all requested minutes).
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
